title: Things to do in Takamatsu: 5 places from gardens to the sea
description: Plan five Takamatsu places: Ritsurin Garden, Tamamo Park, Yashimaji, Shikoku Mura and Kitahama Alley, with rail access, admission advice and a ferry-free route.
relatedQueries: how to get to Yashima from Takamatsu
intro: For a first visit to Takamatsu, focus on five contrasting places: Ritsurin Garden, the castle remains in Tamamo Park, Yashimaji Temple, the historic buildings of Shikoku Mura and the converted warehouses of Kitahama Alley. They introduce designed landscapes, coastal defences, pilgrimage and everyday architecture. All five are on Shikoku, so you can build a rewarding visit without fitting a ferry into an already busy schedule.

Takamatsu is the capital of Kagawa Prefecture, on the northern coast of Shikoku beside the Seto Inland Sea. Think in two groups: the centre and waterfront around the station, and Yashima to the east. Ritsurin needs its own journey. With only one day, choose the places that best match your interests. To explore all five with room for meals and transport, dividing them between two days is more comfortable. That is a pacing recommendation, rather than a requirement for enjoying the city.

quickFacts.label: Location
quickFacts.value: Takamatsu, Kagawa Prefecture, northern Shikoku, Japan.

quickFacts.label: Rail arrival
quickFacts.value: JR Takamatsu; JNTO describes a rapid-train connection from Okayama taking around an hour.

quickFacts.label: Two areas
quickFacts.value: Centre and coast: Tamamo and Kitahama. East: Shikoku Mura and Mount Yashima. Visit Ritsurin separately.

quickFacts.label: Key calendars
quickFacts.value: Shikoku Mura normally closes on Tuesdays; the direct JR Takamatsu to summit bus does not run every day.

quickFacts.label: Suggested scope
quickFacts.value: One day for a selection; two recommended for all five places without adding an island ferry trip.

sections.heading: 1. Ritsurin Garden: a landscape designed to change as you walk
paragraphs: Ritsurin rewards movement rather than a single photographic stop. Six ponds and thirteen landscaped hills create successive compositions against the backdrop of Mount Shiun. Compare open views across the water with the more enclosed passages between pines and bridges. Kagawa Prefecture explains that successive Takamatsu lords developed the garden over more than a century and used it as a retreat. It now has the national designation of a Special Place of Scenic Beauty.

Your first practical decision is which entrance fits your train. JNTO gives an approximately ten-minute walk from Kotoden Ritsurin-Koen Station to the main entrance. From Ritsurinkoen-Kitaguchi on the JR Kotoku Line, the north entrance is about five minutes away on foot. These are different stations and approaches. Look at the garden map on arrival and choose a circuit that finishes near the exit you need for your next journey, rather than discovering at the far end that your train leaves from the other side.

To look more closely, follow changes in height and the different pond views; Hiraiho Hill is one of the viewpoints highlighted by JNTO. If Kikugetsu-tei tea house or a traditional boat ride appeals, check the specific charge and availability before making it the fixed point of your day. Neither is essential to appreciate the garden. Opening times, flowers and evening illuminations need their own checks: a spring photograph or a general description of seasonal events cannot establish what will be available on your date.

sections.heading: 2. Tamamo Park: understanding a castle through its seawater moats
paragraphs: Takamatsu Castle’s site, now Tamamo Park, explains the city’s connection with its former seafront. The defensive system drew seawater into its moats; walls, enclosures and surviving buildings help you understand that relationship. Do not expect an intact main castle keep: the municipal history records its dismantling in 1884. Structures including Tsukimi and Ushitora turrets and Mizute Gate survive. The interest lies in reading the remains and the layout, rather than walking through a fully preserved castle palace.

The city gives a five-minute walk from JR Takamatsu Station and two minutes from Kotoden Takamatsu-Chikko. The West Gate faces those stations; the East Gate is on the car-park and Kagawa Museum side. Gate hours vary by month and do not always match. The current municipal information lists ordinary admission at ¥300, with visitors under eighteen exempt. The park closes from December 29 to 31. If you are visiting around New Year, those dates should determine the order of your plans.

Spend time looking along the moats, comparing the enclosures and examining the pines in Hiunkaku Garden. The present Hiunkaku building dates from 1917 and is mainly used for venue hire. The municipality distinguishes those arrangements and room-by-room works from a visit to the park, so do not assume that a park ticket provides unrestricted interior access. If a specific room or building is the reason for your visit, check its current arrangements. Afterwards, Kitahama fits naturally into the central part of the day without requiring another long journey.

sections.heading: 3. Yashimaji: a pilgrimage temple on Mount Yashima
paragraphs: Yashimaji is Temple 84 on the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage. The pilgrimage association places it in Yashima Higashimachi and describes its principal Kannon image, main hall and historic treasures. This is a religious site with a different purpose from a garden or museum. Approach quietly, leave room for worshippers and follow instructions about photography, circulation and entering buildings. The entrance gate and surroundings provide a worthwhile encounter without assuming that every interior will be open to visitors.

The mountain setting adds another dimension. Shikoku Mura describes Yashima as a flat-topped highland with views towards the Seto Inland Sea islands, Takamatsu and the Sanuki mountains. Keep the experiences separate when planning: reaching the temple does not mean that you have completed every scenic walk on the summit. Choose a short route according to the time available, visibility and your mobility. Do not rely on a guaranteed sunset view or assume that transport downhill will be available whenever you finish.

If you combine the temple with Shikoku Mura, check the Yashima bus and its return journey before heading up. The museum’s access information describes a shuttle linking JR Yashima or Kotoden-Yashima stations with Yashima-Sanjo, with a stop close to the museum. A direct service from JR Takamatsu also runs on specified days, discussed below. Allow for walking between stops and sights, and save the name Yashima-Sanjo: it identifies the upper area, while the railway stations are at the foot of the mountain.

sections.heading: 4. Shikoku Mura: houses and working buildings from four prefectures
paragraphs: At the foot of Yashima, Shikoku Mura brings together thirty-three historic buildings relocated and restored from Shikoku’s four prefectures. The museum explains that they were built between 1603 and 1926 and used in everyday life. They include houses, workshops, rice storehouses, a theatre and a soy-sauce brewery. Compare materials, roofs and the arrangement of rooms to understand the different jobs the buildings performed. The old Kono family house pictured here provides an example of that domestic heritage.

Instead of concentrating on one photogenic corner, choose several buildings with different functions and read their interpretation. A home answers different needs from a storage building or communal space. The site also includes contemporary architecture, such as the gallery designed by Tadao Ando, but a particular exhibition should not be assumed. Check which areas are available during your visit and give the outdoor paths sufficient time. Looking at a single facade from the entrance misses the point of a collection assembled from across the island.

Published hours are 9:30 to 17:00, with last admission at 16:30; the gallery also closes at 16:30. The listed adult admission is ¥2,200. The normal closing day is Tuesday, moving to the following day when Tuesday is a national holiday, with additional temporary closures possible. A November 16, 2026 notice describes walkway improvements without a route closure, although short waits may be necessary. Check the calendar and notices before travelling. The museum gives a five-minute walk from Kotoden-Yashima and ten minutes from JR Yashima.

sections.heading: 5. Kitahama Alley: port warehouses adapted for new uses
paragraphs: Kitahama Alley brings the route back to the scale of a neighbourhood. Its operator describes regenerating warehouses in the port district while retaining their character and finding new commercial uses. Look at that adaptation: older facades, structures and passageways now sit alongside cafés, shops and other businesses. You do not need to treat it as a huge shopping district or expect a special event. It provides a different way to understand Takamatsu’s working and maritime architecture after the former lordly grounds of Tamamo.

The operator lists individual businesses with their own hours and days off. Choose one or two that interest you and check their details; one café’s timetable is not the timetable for the entire complex. This guide’s archive photograph documents the warehouse setting, rather than proving that a particular business or arrangement of tables is unchanged. Leave entrances clear while looking at the exteriors, and ask before taking photographs inside shops or closely photographing other people.

The operator’s address is 4-14 Kitahamacho. Its access page gives approximately thirteen minutes on foot from JR Takamatsu and eleven from Takamatsu-Chikko; Kotoden Kataharamachi is about four minutes away. Treat those as orientation estimates, rather than guaranteed walking times with luggage or stops. Kitahama works well towards the end of the central group of sights. If you plan to eat there, check the establishment first: arriving after the castle does not mean that every kitchen will still be serving.

sections.heading: Organising trains and buses: distinguish the station names
paragraphs: For an arrival from Honshu, JNTO describes JR Takamatsu as around an hour by rapid train from Okayama. Check your date’s connection and allow a sensible margin if you are arriving on another train. Within the city, similar names can refer to different networks or locations: JR Takamatsu and Takamatsu-Chikko are separate stations, as are JR Yashima and Kotoden-Yashima. Save the complete station name, line and intended sight entrance. Doing this in advance prevents an unnecessary walk to Ritsurin’s wrong gate or waiting for the mountain connection at the wrong station.

Kotoden’s Shido Line reaches Kotoden-Yashima from Kawaramachi. For the onward trip to the summit, check the service for your actual date and stop. Kotoden announces a direct JR Takamatsu–Yashima-Sanjo bus with four round trips on its operating days: Saturdays, Sundays, public holidays and the published summer and winter holiday periods. Do not extend that promise to every weekday. Check the current timetable and last return; if the direct bus does not fit, arrange a connection through the Yashima stations before setting out rather than improvising late in the day.

sections.heading: Admission, pacing and decisions to make before setting out
paragraphs: These five places do not operate as one attraction with a combined ticket. Budget separately for Tamamo, Shikoku Mura, Ritsurin and any optional activity or meal. The Tamamo and Shikoku Mura amounts given here come from the public information consulted for this guide; confirm the rates for your date and any age or discount conditions before paying. A boat ride, tea house or exhibition can have different arrangements from the main grounds. Decide which extras matter to you instead of assuming every option is included.

With a single day, Ritsurin, Tamamo and Kitahama make a coherent garden-and-city selection. Another choice is to spend longer around Yashima and Shikoku Mura and reduce the central stops. For all five, a second day helps you avoid reducing the museum to a rushed arrival near its last admission. If you need to avoid steps, slopes or uneven paths, ask each place about the particular route. A nearby railway station or bus to the summit area does not establish that every path and historic building offers step-free access.

itinerary: Central group: start with Ritsurin, choosing the entrance to suit your train. Return towards JR Takamatsu for Tamamo, after checking its calendar and gate hours. Continue to Kitahama Alley for the warehouse setting and a break at an open business. Leave a realistic space for lunch. If you also want an unhurried street walk, avoid filling the same day with every optional paid activity at both the garden and the castle.

Eastern group: choose a day when Shikoku Mura is open. Travel through JR Yashima or Kotoden-Yashima and allow the museum enough time before last admission. Combine it with Yashimaji and a short upper-area walk, reversing the order if the bus timetable makes that more practical. Check the return before starting, and shorten the scenic walk if weather or transport requires it. Do not add an island simply because Takamatsu is a port: a ferry connection changes the margin for the entire day.

faq.question: Can you visit all five Takamatsu places in one day?
faq.answer: Choosing a smaller group is more comfortable for a single day. Ritsurin, Tamamo and Kitahama suit a garden-and-city visit. Yashimaji and Shikoku Mura require travelling east and arranging the mountain connection. We recommend two days for all five, particularly if you want time for interpretation, meals and breaks.

faq.question: Do you need to rent a car to explore Takamatsu?
faq.answer: A car is not essential for this selection. Ritsurin and the foot of Yashima have railway approaches, while Tamamo and Kitahama can be reached on foot from the JR Takamatsu area. The part requiring closer preparation is the shuttle towards the Yashima summit and its return, especially outside the direct service’s operating days.

faq.question: Does the direct bus from Takamatsu to Mount Yashima run daily?
faq.answer: No. Kotoden’s announcement restricts the direct JR Takamatsu service to weekends, public holidays and the published holiday periods. Distinguish this from services involving the Yashima railway stations. Check the current table for your specific day and stop; this guide is not a replacement for an operating timetable.

faq.question: Does Tamamo Park still have the main castle keep?
faq.answer: No. The city records that it was dismantled in 1884. The seawater moats, surviving historic structures, remains and gardens are the focus of a visit. Admission to the park should not be taken to mean that every historic building is open for an interior tour.

faq.question: What should you check for a Tuesday or New Year visit?
faq.answer: Shikoku Mura normally closes on Tuesdays, switching to the following day when Tuesday is a national holiday. Tamamo lists a December 29–31 closure. Kitahama businesses set their own days off. Check those calendars before dividing your visits, and do not infer special openings from announcements for previous years.

conclusion: Takamatsu becomes more rewarding when you distinguish its different settings: the lords’ garden, the coastal castle, the mountain temple, buildings from everyday island life and the port warehouses. Let calendars and transport shape the order, leave room to pause and check optional activities separately. For a wider Japan route, the related Kurashiki, Hiroshima and Kyoto guides offer different contexts without repeating this visit.
